```{r, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(jwcalendarR)
```

`jwc_date` stores a whole civil day as an integer count from Gregorian
0001-01-01. It is not a timestamp and has no time zone. Inputs use strict
`YYYY-MM-DD` syntax or explicit year, month, and day coordinates.

```{r}
x <- civil_date(2024, 2, 29)
x
absolute_day(x)
ordinal_date(x)
iso_week(x)
gregorian_to_julian(x)
julian_day_number(x)
```

Arithmetic has explicit invalid-date handling. For example, adding one month
to January 31 errors by default; `invalid = "previous-valid"` clamps to the
last day of February. No locale or timezone conversion is involved.
